review.overview: PR #403 stages a shared Railway Redis service, adds a typed @package/queue boundary with BullMQ and in-memory adapters, and moves the scraper producers and processor onto it while keeping the legacy scraper-queue. The assumed load is the existing single scheduled scraper service with BullMQ workers and a few producers, not many concurrent writers. The main risks are that the new queue has no volume in the visible plan, the Redis client stops reconnecting after three attempts, and shutdown can drop pending enqueues. The docs also tell operators to cut over immediately, which conflicts with the PR claim that cutover is separately approved.

findings.title: Staged queue writes to a volume the plan does not provision
findings.evidence: The sharedQueue start command writes RDB and AOF to $RAILWAY_VOLUME_MOUNT_PATH, but railway-config.test.mjs expects exactly four resources including only volume.redis-volume, which the legacy queue uses. No distinct volume is attached to sharedQueue in the visible plan.
findings.impact: If the env var is unset the redis-server start command receives --dir with no value and crash-loops. If Railway supplies ephemeral storage instead, AOF and RDB vanish on redeploy and the durable queue claim is false.
findings.recommendation: Attach a new volume to sharedQueue, for example pocket-trash-queue-volume, assert it in railway-config.test.mjs, and never mount redis-volume into two Redis services.

findings.title: Redis client gives up reconnecting after about two seconds
findings.evidence: retryStrategy returns null once times exceeds 3, so ioredis stops reconnecting after roughly 1.75 seconds. BullMQ workers are long-lived and expect the connection to recover.
findings.impact: A Redis restart, failover, or slow Railway deploy leaves the scraper process alive but unable to enqueue or process jobs until someone restarts it. Cron runs then fail silently.
findings.recommendation: Return a capped delay for every attempt on worker connections, and reserve fail-fast retry limits for short-lived commands or tests.

findings.title: Shutdown disconnects before pending commands flush
findings.evidence: close() calls connection.disconnect(), which closes the socket immediately instead of waiting for pending commands to flush.
findings.impact: On SIGTERM during an enqueue or completion ack, the command can be lost. Producers may drop jobs and workers may leave work unacknowledged.
findings.recommendation: Await connection.quit() after closing queues, with a short timeout that falls back to disconnect().

findings.title: Shared queue exposes a public Redis TCP proxy
findings.evidence: sharedQueue copies the legacy tcpProxies: { "6379": {} }, so the new Redis is reachable through a public TCP proxy. The docs say clients should use the private REDIS_URL and never copy the public endpoint.
findings.impact: The shared queue adds another internet-facing Redis endpoint protected only by a password, which increases brute-force and scanning exposure for no stated benefit.
findings.recommendation: Remove the TCP proxy from sharedQueue and keep only the private network endpoint, unless a documented external consumer needs public access.

findings.title: Docs prescribe a cutover the PR says is not approved
findings.evidence: The new paragraph tells operators to point the scraper and Discord bot at ${{pocket-trash-queue.REDIS_URL}}. The PR body says the legacy queue is retained and previews stay on it until a separately approved cutover, and deploy.yml changes no REDIS_URL.
findings.impact: An operator following the docs can switch the scraper to an empty queue before the approved cutover, leaving jobs already in scraper-queue unprocessed with no drain step.
findings.recommendation: State that existing services keep the legacy scraper-queue reference until the cutover PR, and move the switch instruction into that PR.

findings.title: Durability claim has no restart test
findings.evidence: The integration fixture starts Redis with --appendonly no and kills it without a restart. No test exercises the RDB and AOF flags or a Redis restart; railway-config.test.mjs only regex-matches the start command.
findings.impact: A missing volume or wrong persistence flag ships without a failing test, so the core durability claim of this PR is unverified.
findings.recommendation: Add one test that starts Redis with the production persistence flags, writes a key or job, restarts the process, and asserts the data survives. Assert the volume attachment in the Railway test as well.

review.overview: PR #354 adds a normalized Pens catalog schema covering market geography, source provenance and evidence, pens and parts, mechanisms, refill offerings, compatibility, terminology, and product configuration. The review covered the visible Drizzle schema, migration prefix, relations, catalog service, and tests. The main risks are an alias-concept migration that needs a backfill, a schema import cycle, containment cycles, and locking index builds on existing catalog tables.

findings.title: Alias concept_id migration needs a backfill for existing rows
findings.evidence: createAlias now fails when no catalog_terminology_concept matches (`if (!concept) throw new Error(...)`) and inserts only `conceptId`; existing catalog_terminology_alias rows were written with canonical_key and have no concept_id, and the visible migration prefix shows no concept seed or concept_id backfill.
findings.impact: Deploying with existing aliases either fails when concept_id is added NOT NULL or leaves old aliases unreadable through the new concept relation.
findings.recommendation: Seed concepts from existing namespace and key pairs, map every alias to its concept id, then set concept_id NOT NULL in the same migration; add an integration test that starts with a pre-existing alias.

findings.title: Schema modules form an import cycle
findings.evidence: collection.ts imports catalogTerminologyConcept from ./pens.js, while pens.ts imports collectionItem, finishOption, product, productImage, and productMaterial from ./collection.js.
findings.impact: ESM evaluates one side first; any non-lazy use of a table binding can throw 'Cannot access ... before initialization' or produce an undefined table at startup.
findings.recommendation: Move catalogTerminologyConcept into a neutral module imported by both schemas, or define the cross-schema reference only in relations.ts.

findings.title: Market containment accepts cycles
findings.evidence: catalog_market_containment only checks parent_market_id <> child_market_id; nothing prevents A containing B and B containing A, or longer cycles.
findings.impact: Recursive market rollups and ancestor or descendant queries can loop or return a wrong market scope.
findings.recommendation: Reject cycles with a deferred constraint trigger, or store the hierarchy in a closure table and validate inserts in one transaction.

findings.title: Unique constraints on existing catalog tables lock writes
findings.evidence: The PR adds unique("product_id_maker_unique") to product and unique("product_material_id_product_unique") to product_material at line 562, both existing tables.
findings.impact: The migration builds new unique indexes under an exclusive lock; on a large product catalog, writes block for the index build and the deploy can stall.
findings.recommendation: Check table sizes first. If they are large, create the indexes concurrently in a separate migration and attach the constraints afterward.

findings.title: Catalog tests no longer fail on extra product types
findings.evidence: Two exact resolves.toEqual([...]) assertions became resolves.toEqual(expect.arrayContaining([...])), so unexpected rows are ignored.
findings.impact: Duplicate or leaked product types can appear without failing the test, hiding seed and isolation bugs.
findings.recommendation: Filter by the test's maker or type IDs and assert the exact rows, or assert the expected length plus contents.

findings.title: updated_at is never refreshed on update
findings.evidence: entityTimestamps gives updatedAt only defaultNow(); the visible schema and migration define no BEFORE UPDATE trigger.
findings.impact: updated_at stays at insert time unless every service explicitly sets it, so ordering, cache invalidation, and audit views go stale.
findings.recommendation: Add a shared BEFORE UPDATE trigger, or set updated_at in every Pens update path and test it.

findings.title: Serial numbers are validated with trim but stored untrimmed
findings.evidence: collection_item_serial_number_valid uses char_length(trim(serial_number)) between 1 and 200, but serial_number itself is stored as plain text.
findings.impact: '123' and ' 123 ' are accepted as different values, so duplicate serials can coexist and lookups by exact value miss rows.
findings.recommendation: Add a check that serial_number = trim(serial_number), or normalize the value before insert.

review.overview: PR #354 adds the Pens catalog schema: a 1,407-line Drizzle module, a 1,145-line native migration, 587 lines of relations, catalog-service changes, integration tests, and a large schema-diagram update. The visible excerpts show a sound shared-primary-key and provenance design, but market code uniqueness, containment cycles, and alias namespace handling need correction before merge.

findings.title: Market code uniqueness blocks regions that share a country code
findings.evidence: `catalog_market` defines `"code" text NOT NULL CONSTRAINT "catalog_market_code_unique" UNIQUE`; `catalog_market_code_valid` then allows `kind = 'region'` codes of 2-40 characters, so a region code like `CA` cannot coexist with the country code `CA`.
findings.impact: A state or province market such as California or Ontario cannot be stored beside Canada, or must use a non-standard code that breaks code-based lookup.
findings.recommendation: Replace the column UNIQUE with `UNIQUE (kind, code)`, or require region codes to carry a country prefix such as `US-CA` and enforce that format in the CHECK.

findings.title: Region market codes are case-sensitive and not normalized
findings.evidence: The `region` branch of `catalog_market_code_valid` only checks `char_length(trim("code")) between 2 and 40 and "code" <> 'GLOBAL'`; it does not require uppercase, and the unique constraint is case-sensitive, so `us` and `US` both pass and both can be inserted.
findings.impact: Market lookup by code can miss rows depending on casing, and duplicate-looking markets pollute the hierarchy.
findings.recommendation: Add `code = upper(code)` for country and region, or use CITEXT, and compare `upper(code) <> 'GLOBAL'`.

findings.title: Market containment allows cycles and multiple parents
findings.evidence: `catalog_market_containment` has only `PRIMARY KEY (parent_market_id, child_market_id)` and `CHECK (parent_market_id <> child_market_id)`. Rows `(A,B)` and `(B,A)` both satisfy both constraints.
findings.impact: Recursive parent or ancestor queries can loop forever or return duplicate markets; a market can also have multiple parents, which may conflict with a tree model.
findings.recommendation: If containment is a tree, add `UNIQUE (child_market_id)`; otherwise add a recursive cycle check or trigger and document the DAG model.

findings.title: Containment child lookups have no supporting index
findings.evidence: The containment primary key is `(parent_market_id, child_market_id)`; no index begins with `child_market_id`. Finding a market's parents scans the whole table.
findings.impact: Ancestor resolution becomes O(n) per market as the hierarchy grows.
findings.recommendation: Add `CREATE INDEX catalog_market_containment_child_idx ON catalog_market_containment (child_market_id);`.

findings.title: Alias creation hardcodes product-type namespace and input key
findings.evidence: The service looks up the concept with `input.canonicalNamespace` and `canonicalKey`, but the returned row overwrites `canonicalNamespace: "product-type"`; the insert also stores the input key rather than `concept.key`.
findings.impact: Aliases for any other namespace are reported as product-type, and a concept key that differs from the normalized input key splits the alias from its concept.
findings.recommendation: Return the namespace from the concept or input and use `concept.key` for `canonicalKey`; consider dropping the duplicated canonical columns now that `concept_id` exists.

findings.title: Product-type tests weakened to arrayContaining
findings.evidence: `listProductTypes` assertions changed from `resolves.toEqual([...])` to `resolves.toEqual(expect.arrayContaining([...]))` in two places.
findings.impact: Extra or duplicate product types now pass the test; the assertion no longer proves the service returns only the expected set.
findings.recommendation: Keep exact matching against a filtered result, or assert the length plus contents; seed the Pens product types explicitly in the test.

review.overview: PR #354 adds a normalized Pens catalog schema: shared-primary-key pen and part detail tables, mechanisms, refills, compatibility, markets and containment, source listings and evidence, and terminology concepts. It also adds a 1,145-line migration, central relation wiring, service lookup changes, integration tests, and an updated schema diagram. The visible hunks are broadly guarded by checks, but the review found a schema import cycle, non-updating updated_at columns, and a market hierarchy that permits cycles.

findings.title: Circular import between collection and pens schema modules
findings.evidence: collection.ts adds `import { catalogTerminologyConcept } from "./pens.js";`; pens.ts:18-24 imports `collectionItem`, `finishOption`, `product`, `productImage`, and `productMaterial` from `./collection.js`.
findings.impact: ESM finishes one module before the other, so a top-level use of the imported table can throw a temporal-dead-zone error; at minimum, drizzle-kit must resolve a cycle every time it loads the schema.
findings.recommendation: Move the concept table to a neutral module such as catalog-terminology.ts and import it from both schema files, keeping the import graph acyclic.

findings.title: updated_at never changes on row updates
findings.evidence: `entityTimestamps` at pens.ts:28-35 defines `updatedAt: timestamp("updated_at", { withTimezone: true }).defaultNow().notNull()`; there is no `$onUpdate`, and the migration only sets `DEFAULT now()`.
findings.impact: Updates leave updated_at at the creation time, so cache invalidation, audit, and recent-change queries read stale values.
findings.recommendation: Add `.$onUpdate(() => new Date())` to the column or a `BEFORE UPDATE` trigger that assigns `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`.

findings.title: Market containment allows cycles
findings.evidence: `catalog_market_containment` has PRIMARY KEY (parent_market_id, child_market_id) and only `CHECK ("parent_market_id" <> "child_market_id")`; nothing rejects A -> B plus B -> A.
findings.impact: Recursive market nesting or permission inheritance can loop indefinitely, and the hierarchy can store contradictory containment.
findings.recommendation: Reject cycles in an insert/update trigger with a recursive check, or document the acyclic contract and bound traversal depth in every consumer.

findings.title: No reverse index for market containment child
findings.evidence: The containment primary key is `(parent_market_id, child_market_id)`; `child_market_id` has no separate index in the visible migration.
findings.impact: Deleting or re-keying a market forces a sequential scan of containment for the FK check, and child-to-parent lookups are slow.
findings.recommendation: Add `CREATE INDEX catalog_market_containment_child_idx ON catalog_market_containment (child_market_id);`.

findings.title: Composite unique indexes duplicate the primary key
findings.evidence: collection.ts:368 adds `unique("product_id_maker_unique").on(table.id, table.makerId)` and collection.ts:562 adds `unique("product_material_id_product_unique").on(table.id, table.productId)`; both `id` columns are already primary keys.
findings.impact: Each extra unique constraint writes and stores a second B-tree for a uniqueness rule the primary key already enforces; it only pays off if a composite FK targets it.
findings.recommendation: Confirm a composite FK needs these targets; otherwise drop both constraints and keep only the existing primary keys.

findings.title: Region market codes are validated untrimmed
findings.evidence: `catalog_market_code_valid` checks `char_length(trim("code"))` and `"code" <> 'GLOBAL'`, but `code` is stored and uniquely indexed as entered.
findings.impact: `'US '` and `'US'` both pass the region branch and coexist under the unique constraint, so code lookups and joins miss rows.
findings.recommendation: Add `CHECK ("code" = btrim("code"))` or normalize the value before insert, and make the case rule explicit.
